stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: OpenAI accused of ‘aiding and abetting’ Tumbler Ridge mass shooting in dozens of new lawsuits
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman are facing 30 new lawsuits.
The lawsuits allege OpenAI provided 'substantial assistance and encouragement' to a suspect in the Tumbler Ridge mass shooting.
The legal action was filed in a California federal court by students, teachers, and the principal.

stories.title: FTC alleges Amazon illegally made $20 billion by rigging billions of ad auctions
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: The FTC has filed allegations against Amazon regarding its advertising practices.
The core allegation is that Amazon illegally manipulated ad auctions to inflate prices.
The FTC claims Amazon replaced actual auction results with higher prices it set itself, potentially amounting to $20 billion.

stories.title: H3-World: Turning Language Understanding into World Control
stories.author: Yeying Jin
bullet_points: Introduces H3-World, a framework that converts large video generators (like MiniMax-H3) into interactive world models.
Highlights that natural language is emerging as a primary and effective interface for controlling complex AI systems.
Demonstrates that the system allows for precise, temporally grounded control over generated video content using language instructions.

stories.title: Facet-0: A Robotic Foundation Model for Contact-Rich Precise Manipulation
stories.author: Ziwei Wang
bullet_points: Facet-0 is a new robotic foundation model designed for highly precise, contact-rich manipulation tasks.
It uniquely predicts and evaluates the consequences of physical actions by unifying multimodal learning and Reinforcement Learning (RL).
The model integrates causal wrench history with vision-language semantics and kinematic state to enable sub-millimeter assembly.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key AI/ML tags including 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates continued community interest and benchmarking activity around Meta's latest open-source LLM releases.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round includes major investors such as Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is rapidly growing, serving a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.31 achieves significant speed improvements for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speedups reach up to 90% when Gemma 4 is utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these personal AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: Elon Musk’s heterodox robotaxi philosophy gets put to the test
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Tesla is launching its robotaxi service in Austin, Texas, featuring the Cybercab.
The Cybercab is a steering-wheel-free, autonomous vehicle designed as Tesla's future mobility solution.
This rollout marks a significant operational step in Tesla's autonomous driving ambitions.

stories.title: The Army just used a 20-kilowatt laser to take out three drones
stories.author: Fernanda González, wired.com
bullet_points: The U.S. Army has successfully demonstrated the use of a 20-kilowatt laser system.
The technology is designed for tracking and neutralizing hostile drone threats.
This represents a significant advancement in directed energy weapons for defense applications.

stories.title: The Rise of Verbal Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Sambit Sahu
bullet_points: Introduces Verbal Reinforcement Learning (VRL) as a paradigm where natural language serves as a primary feedback channel for improving language agents.
VRL allows for the conveyance of complex information like intent, preferences, and causal structure to AI models.
The field is structured around two axes: when verbal feedback is applied in an agent's lifecycle and what aspects of the agent it modifies.

stories.title: The Structure of Quantization Damage in LLMs: Why the Next Bit Should Be Spent Globally
stories.author: Shekar Ramachandran
bullet_points: The research investigates the uneven accuracy cost associated with Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) in Large Language Models (LLMs).
It proposes a method to intelligently allocate a limited additional precision budget to mitigate quantization damage across different layers.
The study validates its findings across 9 open-weight models spanning 4 architecture families using causal mixed-precision intervention.

stories.title: NashDreamer: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning for Zero-Sum Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Viliam Lisý
bullet_points: Introduces NashDreamer, a novel Model-Based Reinforcement Learning (MBRL) approach.
Addresses the significant challenge of applying MBRL to competitive, imperfect-information games (IIGs).
Argues for the necessity of centralized model learning to overcome identifiability barriers in multi-agent settings.

stories.title: Mistral now trains on user input by default, except on enterprise tier
stories.author: teekert
bullet_points: Mistral AI has updated its model training process to incorporate user input by default.
This change applies to standard user tiers, indicating a shift in data utilization for model improvement.
Enterprise customers retain the option to opt-out of having their input used for training.

stories.title: WebLLM: high-performance in-browser LLM inference engine
stories.author: saikatsg
bullet_points: Introduces WebLLM, a new engine designed for high-performance LLM inference directly in the browser.
Signifies a move toward decentralized or client-side AI processing, reducing reliance on large cloud APIs.
Addresses the technical challenge of running large language models efficiently within web environments.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware platforms.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NYC bans AI use for students until they reach high school
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: NYC is implementing a one-year ban on AI use in classrooms for younger students.
The moratorium targets students in grades 2-8, affecting approximately 600,000 public school students.
The policy, announced by Mayor Zohran Mamdani, is part of broader limits on digital devices.

stories.title: Tado’s new thermostat is designed as a Nest killer
stories.author: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy
bullet_points: Tado is launching its Smart Thermostat X (2nd gen) to compete directly in the European smart thermostat market.
The launch is strategically timed following Google's exit from the European thermostat market, which impacted existing users.
Tado is specifically targeting European users who were previously invested in Nest thermostats.

stories.title: Acer’s new MacBook Air rival is nearly a pound lighter than Apple’s laptop
stories.author: Antonio G. Di Benedetto
bullet_points: Acer has released the Swift Blade 14, positioning it as a direct competitor to the MacBook Air.
The new laptop emphasizes portability, weighing in at just 1.76 pounds (799g) and being extremely thin.
The announcement highlights a competitive push in the premium, ultrabook segment against Apple's established market leader.

stories.title: Is Russia's rival to Starlink failing? Here's what we know.
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: The article discusses potential failures within Rassvet, a satellite system positioned as a rival to Starlink.
Initial data suggests at least three of the first 32 Rassvet satellites have experienced outright failures.
The news points to potential reliability issues with the competing satellite constellation.

stories.title: BGP hijack infecting networks caused by a comedy of errors that’s not funny at all
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: The article discusses a BGP hijacking incident that negatively impacted production software.
The incident is characterized as a 'comedy of errors,' suggesting human or configuration mistakes were involved.
The piece aims to draw lessons from the event regarding network security and BGP vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Efficient SWE Agent Benchmarking via Trajectory-Aware Evaluation
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: Addresses the high computational cost of evaluating Software Engineering (SWE) AI agents on complex tasks.
Proposes PTA-IRT, a new framework that moves beyond simple pass/fail metrics to analyze *how* agents solve problems.
Integrates Trajectory-Aware evaluation with Item Response Theory (IRT) for more nuanced performance assessment.

stories.title: CordisBench: Can Language Models Reason About Component Lifecycles in Dynamic Agent Harnesses?
stories.author: Dimitri Kachler
bullet_points: Introduces CordisBench, a new 1,200-question benchmark for evaluating language model reasoning.
Focuses on the complex lifecycle reasoning required when language models dynamically alter their own execution environments (dynamic agent harnesses).
Tests models' ability to track dependency propagation and cleanup across changing software components.

stories.title: Mechanism Design for Alignment and Control
stories.author: Stephen Morris
bullet_points: Presents a mechanism design framework for interacting with AI agents whose preferences and capabilities are unknown.
The framework aims to incentivize agents to be honest and obedient when acting on behalf of a designer.
Introduces a 'one-sided imitation structure' leading to a revelation principle and characterization of implementable policies.

stories.title: Designing Proactive Thought Partners for Writing
stories.author: Chin-Chia Hsu
bullet_points: The paper addresses the limitations of current AI writing tools, which offer only generic textual assistance like autocomplete.
It introduces the concept of 'proactive thought partners'—AI agents designed to offer customizable, higher-level cognitive support during the writing process.
The research focuses on mapping the design space for these advanced AI agents to better match diverse writer needs across different stages (ideation to revision).

stories.title: Scaling Near-Optimal SFT-RL Annotation Budget Allocation from Small to Large LLMs
stories.author: Bryan Kian Hsiang Low
bullet_points: Addresses the open problem of optimally allocating a fixed annotation budget between Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) during LLM post-training.
Moves beyond broad trend observations to propose a principled framework for characterizing near-optimal SFT-RL allocation.
Investigates whether the optimal SFT-RL ratio remains consistent when scaling from small to large Language Models (LLMs).

stories.title: Selective Agent Guidance via Entropy: Learning Autonomous Policies from Imperfect VLM Teachers
stories.author: Bernardo Magnini
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitations of using large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) directly as decision-making policies due to high cost and brittleness.
The proposed framework, SAGE (Selective Agent Guidance via Entropy), aims to learn an efficient, autonomous policy from an imperfect VLM teacher.
SAGE strategically queries the VLM only when the learning agent exhibits uncertainty, improving efficiency.

stories.title: From Confusion to Clarity: Confusion-Aware Retrieval and Knowledge Injection for Text Classification
stories.author: Jayasimha Talur
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in LLM text classification when dealing with taxonomies having many semantically similar labels.
Critiques the standard top-K retrieval method, noting it reduces candidates but fails to help the model distinguish between similar options.
Proposes a 'Confusion-Aware Retrieval and Knowledge Injection' approach to improve classification accuracy in complex label spaces.

stories.title: Beyond Scores: Understanding LLM-as-a-Judge Mechanisms in Summarization Evaluation
stories.author: Ming Jiang
bullet_points: The paper investigates the internal mechanisms of LLM-as-a-Judge systems used to evaluate Natural Language Generation (NLG) quality.
It employs an eight-attack perturbation taxonomy to mechanistically probe how LLMs assign ratings across Readability and Adequacy.
This research addresses the lack of understanding regarding how LLM evaluators function when used as automated scoring tools or training signals.

stories.title: Scaling Near-Optimal SFT-RL Annotation Budget Allocation from Small to Large LLMs
stories.author: Bryan Kian Hsiang Low
bullet_points: Addresses the open problem of optimally allocating a fixed annotation budget between Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) during LLM post-training.
Moves beyond broad trend observations by proposing a principled framework to characterize near-optimal SFT-RL allocation.
Investigates whether the optimal allocation ratio remains consistent when scaling from smaller to larger Large Language Models (LLMs).

stories.title: Selective Agent Guidance via Entropy: Learning Autonomous Policies from Imperfect VLM Teachers
stories.author: Bernardo Magnini
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitations of using large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) directly as decision-making policies due to high cost and brittleness.
A new framework, SAGE (Selective Agent Guidance via Entropy), is proposed to learn an efficient, autonomous policy from an imperfect VLM teacher.
SAGE intelligently queries the expensive VLM only when the learning agent exhibits uncertainty, improving efficiency.

stories.title: Can LLMs Discover Scientific Laws in Real and Parallel Worlds?
stories.author: Jingbo Shang
bullet_points: The paper addresses the open question of whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can genuinely discover scientific laws.
It critiques current evaluation methods for LLM scientific discovery, noting they often rely on simplified synthetic settings or reuse existing published work.
The research situates LLMs within the established scientific process of hypothesis generation, testing, and refinement.

stories.title: A Mathematical Theory of Reusable Neural Bases for Network Compression
stories.author: Binshuai Wang
bullet_points: Addresses the critical memory and parameter efficiency bottleneck in large AI models.
Introduces the Linear Reusable Neural Bases Architecture (LRNBA) for network compression.
The core concept involves representing network blocks as linear combinations of a shared set of bases, inspired by RNNs.

stories.title: Beyond Scores: Understanding LLM-as-a-Judge Mechanisms in Summarization Evaluation
stories.author: Ming Jiang
bullet_points: Investigates the internal mechanisms of LLM-as-a-Judge systems used to evaluate Natural Language Generation (NLG) quality.
Employs an eight-attack perturbation taxonomy across Readability and Adequacy dimensions to probe these evaluators.
Addresses the lack of understanding regarding how LLMs assign ratings when used as automated scoring tools in summarization.

stories.title: Efficient SWE Agent Benchmarking via Trajectory-Aware Evaluation
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: Addresses the high cost of evaluating software engineering (SWE) agents on realistic, multi-step tasks.
Introduces PTA-IRT, a novel framework combining Trajectory-Awareness with Item Response Theory (IRT).
Moves beyond simple pass/fail metrics by analyzing *how* agents solve problems during code exploration and modification.

stories.title: CordisBench: Can Language Models Reason About Component Lifecycles in Dynamic Agent Harnesses?
stories.author: Dimitri Kachler
bullet_points: Introduces CordisBench, a new benchmark designed to test language models' ability to reason about component lifecycles.
The benchmark focuses on 'dynamic agent harnesses,' where LLMs can modify their own execution environment, creating complex dependency challenges.
It tests models on identifying affected components and predicting state changes resulting from local plugin modifications within a controlled runtime environment.

stories.title: The Rise of Verbal Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Sambit Sahu
bullet_points: Introduces Verbal Reinforcement Learning (VRL) as a new paradigm where natural language serves as a primary feedback mechanism for language agents.
VRL allows agents to receive feedback conveying intent, preferences, and causal structure in a human-interpretable format.
The field is structured around two axes: when verbal feedback is applied in an agent's lifecycle and what aspect of the agent it modifies.

stories.title: StudentSim: Training LLM-based Student Simulators
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: StudentSim proposes using LLM-based student simulators to gather data on effective personalized tutoring strategies.
Current simulator approaches are limited: state-tracking models lack explanatory depth, while LLM role-play lacks competence matching.
The research addresses the need for scalable, less costly methods to determine optimal guidance for individual student learning profiles.

stories.title: Designing Proactive Thought Partners for Writing
stories.author: Chin-Chia Hsu
bullet_points: The research focuses on developing 'proactive thought partners' for writing, moving beyond simple autocomplete.
These AI agents aim to provide customizable, higher-level cognitive support tailored to the writer's specific needs.
The paper explores the design space for AI tools that offer timely and context-aware assistance throughout the writing process (ideation to revision).

stories.title: The Structure of Quantization Damage in LLMs: Why the Next Bit Should Be Spent Globally
stories.author: Shekar Ramachandran
bullet_points: The research investigates the uneven accuracy degradation caused by Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) in Large Language Models (LLMs).
The study proposes a method to intelligently allocate a small additional precision budget to mitigate quantization damage.
It tests hypotheses across 9 open-weight models and 4 architecture families using causal mixed-precision intervention as a ground truth.

stories.title: Closing Cost-Quality Gap in Document VLMs: Difficulty-Aware Data Curation and Quality-Adjusted Deployment Economics
stories.author: Aleksandr Ivanov
bullet_points: Addresses the high cost and quality gap in using Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for extracting structured data from massive document volumes in regulated industries.
Proposes a solution using a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) VLM architecture, fine-tuned on proprietary and open-domain data, to improve efficiency.
Highlights the practical challenge where existing high-quality open-source models are too expensive to deploy compared to human annotation.

stories.title: Scaling Near-Optimal SFT-RL Annotation Budget Allocation from Small to Large LLMs
stories.author: Bryan Kian Hsiang Low
bullet_points: Addresses the open problem of optimally dividing a fixed annotation budget between Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) during LLM post-training.
Moves beyond broad trend observations by proposing a principled framework to characterize near-optimal SFT-RL allocation.
Investigates whether the optimal SFT-RL ratio remains consistent when scaling from small to large Language Models (LLMs).

stories.title: Execution Trees, Not More Logs: A Better Debugging Model for AI Agents
stories.author: raju_dandigam
bullet_points: Proposes 'Execution Trees' as an advanced debugging model for AI agents.
Argues that traditional flat logs are insufficient for tracing causality in complex AI operations.
Focuses on improving observability and understanding the root cause of agent behavior.

stories.title: Streamline Publishing with a Claude Code Skill
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: Introduces a Claude Code skill designed to automate content syndication from a single Markdown file.
The skill handles multi-platform formatting for Dev.to, AWS Builder Center, Medium, and LinkedIn.
It includes pre-shipping checks and debugging tools to ensure content integrity across different publishing APIs.

stories.title: What happens to technical debt when AI makes code cheap?
stories.author: jennapederson
bullet_points: Examines the future impact of AI-driven code generation on technical debt.
Poses a critical question about how AI might alter the traditional management of legacy code.
Suggests a shift in software development practices as code creation becomes cheaper.

stories.title: I Found 3 Security Vulnerabilities in My Own AI Agent's Tool Access
stories.author: dannwaneri
bullet_points: The article details the discovery of three security vulnerabilities within a personal AI agent's tool access.
The project, named GeoMart, was built as part of OpenAI's WebMCP Challenge.
This highlights practical security challenges in developing and deploying AI agents with external tool access.
